title: Avoiding Oppression and Stinginess
summary: The Prophet Muhammad warned against oppression and stinginess, citing their severe consequences in the hereafter.
translation: In the matter of oppression, there is a hadith from Jabir bin Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) mentioning two evils, one of which is oppression. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'Avoid oppression, as oppression will cause darkness on the Day of Resurrection.' This means that on the Day of Resurrection, the oppressor will be surrounded by darkness; they will lack the light that believers will have, as mentioned in the Quran: "Their light will run forward before them and by their right hands." The oppressors will be deprived of this light. Some scholars suggest that 'darkness' here means suffering, hardships, and trials—that oppressors will be engulfed in pain. The hadith also includes, 'Avoid stinginess, for stinginess destroyed those before you. It led them to shed blood and to make lawful what was forbidden.' The Messenger (peace be upon him) indicated that extreme love for wealth leads a person to disregard respect and dignity towards others, causing them to overlook distinctions between lawful and unlawful, leading them to violence. Allah’s beloved Prophet (peace be upon him) therefore warned Muslims against these evils, emphasizing that oppression is fundamentally harmful. Allah states, 'And the wrongdoers will have no devoted friends and no one will advocate for them.' Another hadith by Abu Huraira (may Allah be pleased with him) mentions that justice will be served on the Day of Resurrection as a hornless goat will receive retribution from a horned goat, illustrating that human oppression will certainly be compensated.
